content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm using a counter and need its output to turn off when the counter is reset. Currently, the circuit only resets the counter value and not the output (Q1). Can someone help me identify the issue? Thank you, [user_name]

Hi [user_name], for future questions, please share your original circuit to make it easier to assist you. In my program, everything seems fine: when I activate I1, the counter increases from 0 to a set value and if it exceeds 5, Q1 switches ON. When I deactivate I1, the counter resets to 0 and Q1 switches OFF. Is there something about your desired function that I might be misunderstanding? Best regards, [user_name]

Hello all, Thank you for your help. I found the issue—it was a mistake in setting the 'off threshold' for the counter (I had set it to 0 instead of 1). I'm now facing a new problem: I1 is an object detection sensor that activates when an object arrives. It's hard to set the counter's on and off thresholds if the conveyor speed changes. Is there a way to implement teach-in settings or another solution for the counter or generator? I'm eager to hear your suggestions. Thank you, [user_name]

Hello, Remember that a pulse at the 'R' input of the counter resets the value to zero and also sets the output to OFF—this works regardless of whether the 'OFF' parameter is greater than 0. I wasn't clear on your second question; could you describe in detail what signals you have or want at the input and what your intended outcome is, using words instead of [product_name] functions? Best regards, [user_name]

Hi everyone, thanks for responding. I know how the counter settings should work, but during simulation, the output doesn't turn off when I reset I1 (it only resets when I adjust the off threshold to 1, and I'm not sure why). In my project, I need to verify if a box contains three small aluminum bags—three bags is OK, fewer than three is not OK. I'm using two sensors: one detects the box (S1), and the other detects the bags inside via proximity (S2). If there are three bags, S2's output is continuous; if fewer, the S2 output turns ON and OFF randomly. Please refer to the attached file for my approach and the issue. Thank you and awaiting your reply, [user_name]

Hi [user_name], I couldn't view the details of your circuit in the pdf file. If your conveyor speed is always constant, your method for checking the number of bags is acceptable. However, if the speed changes, you'll need a different approach. You could determine a characteristic value 'm' by using the formula: 'time S1_on / time S2_on = constant.' In your application, that could mean '6 pulses of S1 / 4 pulses of S2 = 1.5 = m.' While I would use a different circuit concept, here's how you might improve your design: 1. Increase the pulse frequency to enhance resolution. 2. By setting the pulse generator parameters so '(TH+TL) for S1 = m * (TH+TL) for S2,' the counter values for both should match when the right number of bags are present. 3. Define the 'ON' parameter of the counter for S1 to reference the counter value for S2. The counter output for S1 will be '1' when there are fewer than three bags, triggering an alarm. 4. Before connecting the alarm to the output, use an AND block with the inverted S1 signal so the alarm is active only during pauses between boxes. I hope this helps you create a working solution for your application. Best regards, [user_name]
Dear [user_name], Thank you very much for your assistance. Best wishes, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: The user initially misunderstood how the counter's reset function operates in [company_name] modules, believing it only clears the count without affecting output. After resolving a threshold setting issue, new challenges emerged in adjusting thresholds due to varying conveyor speed, making manual adjustments impractical. The conversation highlights a need for clearer guidance and flexible options when configuring counters for dynamic industrial environments.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects the counter reset to reliably turn off the output and hopes for a simple teach-in mechanism to handle varying conveyor speeds. Overall, they seek easier adaptation of control logic to real-world changes without frequent manual adjustments.
